summary: Christmas hero episode on Ukrainian anarchist Nestor Makhno, a former serf's son and teenage militant who built peasant communes around Huliaipole and led a guerrilla army against Austro-German occupiers, the Whites and the Bolsheviks from 1917 to 1921.

evidence.note: Makhno's birth in October to former serfs; year garbled in transcript, 1888 from general knowledge
extended framing of Ukraine as a colonized land, land grants to nobles and settlers, serfdom
anarchist group turns to armed expropriations and shootouts with police in 1906-07
death sentence commuted to hard labor; years in tsarist prison reading anarchist theory
freed after the 1917 revolution and returns to organize his hometown
segment on Mennonite landowners forming an armed militia alongside the occupiers
flees to Moscow and meets Lenin before sneaking back into Ukraine
White Army pogroms and reprisals against peasants and Jewish communities
Red Army outlaws Makhno; Cheka purges in retaken towns
final war with the Bolsheviks ends in 1921; escape to Poland then exile
last years spent ill and depressed in Paris
death in Paris; year garbled in transcript, 1934 from general knowledge

notes: Hero format (2020 Christmas non-bastard). Birth and death years garbled in transcript; 1888 and 1934 from general knowledge. Catherine the Great, Cossack and serfdom history is background and not counted in covered_span. Main span uses 1917-1921, though the 1906-1908 militant phase also gets long airtime. Poland and Paris exile brief; PL omitted. Tsar Nicholas II and Bloody Sunday get a few minutes (monarchy-empire left out).
